# NOTE: the draft row expected `string&re(...)`; the probe shows the
# implied-kind rule wins, and the promoted row records what the engines
# agree on rather than what the draft predicted.
# Distinct patterns ACCUMULATE (sorted by source in canon) and are never
# simplified: deciding one pattern subsumes another is regex
# containment, which the algebra deliberately does not do. Emptiness
# stays approximate -- sound, incomplete -- so two `re` atoms are never

# Atom order in canon: kind, lower bound, upper bound, neq, re.
# Domain and shape: a pattern is a STRING membership test, so it mixes
# emptily with the numeric domain and refuses every non-string peer.
# THE PORTABLE SUBSET. A pattern must mean the same thing in both
# engines, so it is checked against one shared syntactic subset
# go/constraint.go) BEFORE either host engine compiles it. Refusal is
# the registered `constraint_pattern` code. As with every other invalid
# atom (errc-invalid-atom-residual), the code is raised when the
# residual is DRIVEN in a meet; on its own it is merely non-generable.
# ABBREVIATIONS ARE NORMALISED, NOT REFUSED (ADR-003). Aontu DEFINES
# what each abbreviation means and rewrites both hosts to it, so neither
# Before this, `\\A` was an anchor in RE2 and a literal "A" in JavaScript
# (so `re("\\A") & "x"` held in Go and failed in TypeScript), and `\\s`
# matched U+00A0 in JavaScript but not in Go. Both are now single-valued.
# The definition BITES: U+00A0 is whitespace to JavaScript and not to
# RE2, and Aontu's \\s excludes it in both. A non-breaking space in a
# config value is a mistake to catch, not a space to accept silently.
# Canon renders the pattern AS WRITTEN, never the normalised form: canon
# round-trips source, and G6's hash will be taken over canon.
# What normalisation cannot reach, and why refusal is still right there:
# a construct one engine simply lacks (there is nothing to rewrite it
# to), a spelling difference that changes meaning wholesale, or a
# difference of COST rather than meaning.

# code point, TWO UTF-16 units) in Go and refused it in TypeScript --

# `\-` is a range separator inside a character class and a syntax error
# outside one under the `u` flag -- while RE2 accepts it in both
# positions. Refused outside a class so the two ports agree.
# QUANTIFIER NESTING is refused, and this rule is about TIME rather than
# meaning. `(a+)+$` against 29 a-characters and a `!` took 45 SECONDS in
# TypeScript and 0.065s under RE2, growing exponentially: a regex match
# is counted by no evaluator budget (docs/trust.md clause 2), so an
# untrusted schema could stall the evaluator indefinitely. Refusing the
# shape keeps the termination clause true in the port that has the
# problem. `(?:a|b)+` is refused too, though safe -- deciding that two
# branches cannot both match is real work; write `[ab]+`.
